Then, however, 'Noddy' Edwards, who had been strolling somewhere in the seventies began to make up places at a most alarming rate. He passed Ken and flogged himself until the funnel was reached to complete our scoring four and,as it at first appeared, to provide us with a Championship place.

Alan Morrison gave away a mere second on the next stage, and with Ken Redwood increasing our lead by a further ½ minute on the third leg 'Noddy' Edwards set off on the final stage with a very comfortable lead.
Eugene Simmons was the first of our quartet to climb the steep priory hill and afer 8 minutes 45 seconds handed over to "Noddy" Edwards in 7th place, 12secs behind Mitcham and 12 ahead of Reading.

"Noddy" Edwards was in hot pursuit of Bicourt throughout and it would seem that he is running into form for the Southern & National just as he did last year; few will forget his fine effort in the latter event.

He joined in the race after a short distance and finished fourth but did not, of course, score. "Noddy" Edwards and 15 years old Ron Hayes filled the breach admirably, however, and we finished third once again.

Noddy Edwards, as usual, ran a blinder when most needed and Eugene Simmonds was his usual consistent self. John Leaver backed up particularly well to close the team in with 357 points which gave us a praiseworthy 11th place.
Noddy Edwards had a real battle on stage 3 and handed over to Bernard Merry for the final circuit just 6 seconds in arrears. However, Bernard's task was hopeless against the class of D.
